conventions.convention: An FLRW datum has c>0, a nonempty open real interval I, a connected boundaryless smooth three-manifold Σ, k∈{-1,0,1}, Ric(γ)=2kγ, and a smooth positive scale factor a. Nonemptiness of Σ is not required.
The product metric is g=-c²dt²+a²γ, the time orientation is ∂t, the unit comoving field is n=c⁻¹∂t, and the proper-time velocity is U=cn=∂t. Thus div(n)=3H/c whereas div(U)=3H.
The spatial Riemann four-tensor is γ(R(X,Y)Z,W), and the curvature operator is ∇X∇Y−∇Y∇X−∇[X,Y]. The normalized round sphere has positive sectional curvature.
The Friedmann-system datum allows any real curvature parameter k and smooth real density and pressure, without positivity or an equation of state. Constants c and G_N are positive and Λ is constant.
With (F) fixed, (S) and (A) are equivalent. Deriving (A) from (F) and (C) by division requires H≠0; deriving (C) from (F) and (A) does not.

The physical cosmological model selects one of the three standard complete simply connected nonempty spatial models, with either vacuum or a homogeneous comoving perfect fluid and an explicit equation of state. This ansatz and the field law are adopted assumptions.

In the physical reading, t and t_* have units seconds, a and A metres, c metres per second, H inverse seconds, Λ inverse square metres, and ε and p joules per cubic metre. The barotropic parameters w and q are dimensionless.

A ray is future null and affinely parametrized; its observer energy is E=-c g(V,n). Redshift is defined by 1+z=E_E/E_R. Positive constant rescaling of the tangent changes energies but not their ratio.
The geometry suppliers carry inherited countable choice AC_ω; the local finite calculations assert no additional choice principle.

load_bearing.statement: For c>0, an FLRW model datum is (I,Σ,γ,k,a) with I a nonempty open interval, (Σ,γ,k) a spatial model datum, and a:I→(0,∞) smooth; its metric is g=-c²dt²+a²γ, comoving field n=c⁻¹∂t, and Hubble parameter H=ȧ/a.
In product charts x⁰=t, Γ⁰₀₀=Γ⁰₀ᵢ=Γ⁰ᵢ₀=Γⁱ₀₀=0, Γ⁰ᵢⱼ=aȧγᵢⱼ/c², Γⁱ₀ⱼ=Γⁱⱼ₀=Hδⁱⱼ, and Γⁱⱼₖ equals the spatial Levi-Civita symbol. These list all potentially nonzero families.
For an FLRW datum in product charts, Ric₀₀=-3ä/a, Ric₀ᵢ=0, Ricᵢⱼ=((aä+2ȧ²)/c²+2k)γᵢⱼ; S=6(ä/(ac²)+H²/c²+k/a²); G₀₀=3(ȧ²+kc²)/a², G₀ᵢ=0, and Gᵢⱼ=-((2aä+ȧ²)/c²+k)γᵢⱼ.
For the specified smooth datum, (F) is H²+kc²/a²=8πG_Nε/(3c²)+Λc²/3; (A) is ä/a=-4πG_N(ε+3p)/(3c²)+Λc²/3; (C) is ε̇+3H(ε+p)=0; (S) is -(2aä+ȧ²)/c²-k+Λa²=8πG_Npa²/c⁴, each throughout I.

For the adopted homogeneous cosmological model in its vacuum or comoving perfect-fluid sector, the field equation holds on spacetime if and only if (F) and (A) hold for its scalar data. If the field equation holds, (C) holds; vacuum has ε=p=0.
For a smooth Riemannian three-manifold and real k, constant sectional curvature k, Ric(γ)=2kγ, and R(X,Y)Z=k(γ(Y,Z)X−γ(X,Z)Y) are equivalent. Under these conditions S=6k and Ric₀=0.

For a future affinely parametrized null ray in the adopted FLRW model, a(t)Vᵗ is constant, E=-c g(V,n)>0, E_R/E_E=a(t_E)/a(t_R), and the defined redshift satisfies 1+z=a(t_R)/a(t_E). The ratios are unchanged by positive constant tangent rescaling.

In the adopted flat vacuum model, Λ>0 gives a(t)=A exp(c√(Λ/3)(t−t₀)) on all of R satisfying (F), (A), and hence the field equations, for every A>0 and t₀∈R. For Λ<0 no smooth positive scale factor on a nonempty open interval satisfies (F).

concerns.concern: Definition (c) says: 'for k≠0 the normalized condition (a) is preserved only when λ=1'. Definition (a) does not exclude Σ=∅. On the allowed empty connected three-manifold, γ and every rescaling are the unique empty metric and Ric(γ)=2kγ is vacuous for every k. Taking k=1 and λ=2 contradicts the claimed necessity of λ=1. The nonempty standard physical models are unaffected.

The scale-redundancy remark says: 'for k=±1 it is a normalized datum only when λ=1'. The datum permits Σ=∅. On that manifold the rescaled empty metric still satisfies the normalized Ricci condition with k=1 or k=-1 for every λ>0. The computed unnormalized presentation parameter k'=λ²k is valid, but the asserted impossibility of a normalized datum is not valid at the stated empty-domain scope.

Fact L3 says: 'a nonzero vector V is future-directed exactly when g(V,∂t)<0'. The cited definition restricts this criterion to nonzero causal vectors. At any point take V=∂t+(2c/a)∂₁ in the Cartesian flat chart: g(V,∂t)=-c²<0 but g(V,V)=3c²>0, so V is spacelike and has no future-directed designation under that supplier. The actual constructed ray is null, so its computation remains sound; the factual assertion nevertheless overstates the cited definition.

Proof 4.1 says 'the empty and low-dimensional cases do not arise because Σ is a three-manifold'. Three-dimensionality excludes low-dimensional tangent spaces at existing points but does not exclude the empty three-manifold under the suppliers' conventions. The tensor identities remain valid vacuously there; the explanatory sentence is inaccurate.

alerts.finding: Fact L3 in ex-gr-cosmological-redshift-interface-record-window says 'a nonzero vector is future-directed exactly when g(V,∂t)<0'. The supplier def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects defines this test only for nonzero causal vectors. In its flat FLRW chart, V=∂t+(2c/a)∂₁ has negative pairing with ∂t but positive squared norm 3c², hence is spacelike. The example establishes nullness for its actual W before using the criterion, so its ray and redshift calculation are unaffected, but L3 is false at its written unrestricted scope.

seams_checked.note: The perfect-fluid stress tensor, conservation equivalence and direct Einstein field law are used with the stated smoothness, constants and nonempty domain. The physical postulate selects nonempty standard models; continuity is also derived directly without dividing by H.

The tensor, Lorentzian-signature, inverse-metric, connection and SI suppliers are used with matching conventions. Mathematical FLRW data retain the suppliers' allowance of empty manifolds; the resulting local normalization concerns are recorded separately.
The Levi-Civita formula, tensor derivative, proper-time normalization and affine null-ray rule are retained. The field equations are not used to justify the adopted light or clock coupling.

Observer energy is exactly -c g(P,n), and positivity is applied to future causal tangents. The expansion lemma explicitly qualifies the observer-congruence designation by Σ≠∅, matching the nonempty-domain supplier.
Curvature sign, loop-index order, Ricci contraction and Einstein tensor agree with the opened suppliers. The component calculations preserve those conventions.

The explicit-ray example's L3 extends the future-direction criterion from nonzero causal vectors to all nonzero vectors. Its actual null ray satisfies the missing hypothesis, but the cited proposition is overstated.
The observer-energy definition and normalization n=c⁻¹∂t are used exactly, giving E=c²Vᵗ and the stated energy ratio.

The architecture and research queue identify the FLRW theorem as restricted comoving-observer redshift content. They retain the missing apparatus, calibration and statistical-analysis obligations and treat the pointers as nonlogical status references.

The worked interface example applies de Sitter clause (a) with Λ=3H²/c²>0 and the redshift theorem to its explicitly checked affine future null ray. Its illustrative interval is not presented as a confidence set or measurement. The separate causal-definition overstatement in its L3 is routed as an alert.
